topic: How would the 0.25 dB passband loss affect link budget margins in low-noise satellite receiver frontends?
consensus_response: A 0.25 dB passband loss compromises the system's ability to detect and decode signals, reducing link budget margins due to increased noise and interference. This is because the passband loss directly affects the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), leading to a decrease in available power for reliable communication. The reduced SNR increases bit error rates and potential service unavailability, impacting system capacity and reliability. In low-noise satellite receiver frontends, a 0.25 dB passband loss would increase noise figure by approximately 1-2 dB, compromising system performance.
